value.body: An agronomist advises farmers on growing healthier crops — soil health, nutrients, irrigation and pest control. Seed, fertiliser and crop-protection companies, agritech start-ups, farmer producer organisations and food companies hire them. Much of the work is in the field: visiting farms, running demonstration plots and keeping records.

items.label: Work setting
items.value: Mostly field-based in rural areas, with regular travel

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as a field or development officer in an agri-input company, agritech firm or FPO support organisation. Knowing the local language and crops of the region is a strong advantage.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Basic data recording on mobile apps

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior agronomist, product development or research roles, regional technical lead.
An M.Sc Agriculture is common for research-oriented agronomy roles.
Work follows crop seasons, with busy periods around sowing and harvest.
